title: First Word Bismillahs Blessing Through A Comparison And A Warning To The Nafs

questions.question: What words does the passage say we should begin good things with?
questions.answer: We should begin with saying Allah’s name.

questions.question: Why is this phrase called special for Muslims?
questions.answer: It is a sign of Islam.

questions.question: In the story, where were the two men traveling?
questions.answer: They were traveling through a desert.

questions.question: Why did a traveler need the name and protection of a leader in that desert?
questions.answer: So he could be safer from harm and get what he needed.

questions.question: How were the two travelers different in their manners?
questions.answer: One was humble, and the other was proud.

questions.question: What did the humble traveler do before going on?
questions.answer: He traveled under the name of a chief.

questions.question: What happened when robbers met the humble traveler?
questions.answer: They left him alone.

questions.question: How did people in the tents treat the humble traveler?
questions.answer: They treated him with respect.

questions.question: What happened to the proud traveler who went alone?
questions.answer: He faced many troubles, felt afraid, and had to beg.

questions.question: In the comparison, who is the traveler in real life?
questions.answer: A person, especially the nafs, is the traveler.

questions.question: In the comparison, what does the desert stand for?
questions.answer: It stands for this world.

questions.question: Why does the passage say a person needs Allah’s name in this world?
questions.answer: Because people are weak, needy, and surrounded by many troubles.

questions.question: What does saying Allah’s name connect a weak person to?
questions.answer: It connects the person to Allah’s power and mercy.

questions.question: What example is given to show how a person acts when saying Allah’s name?
questions.answer: It is like joining the army and acting under the law and government.

questions.question: How does that army example help us understand courage?
questions.answer: It shows that the person does not fear people when acting with rightful support.

questions.question: What is one main lesson of the whole passage?
questions.answer: We should begin our actions with Allah’s name and trust Him.

questions.question: What is the first teaching in this passage about doing good things?
questions.answer: Good things should start with Allah’s name.

questions.question: The passage says this phrase is a sign of what faith?
questions.answer: It is a sign of Islam.

questions.question: What kind of story is used to teach the lesson?
questions.answer: A comparison story about a journey in the desert.

questions.question: What danger did travelers face in the desert?
questions.answer: They could be attacked by bandits.

questions.question: What other problem did travelers have besides danger?
questions.answer: They had many needs to take care of.

questions.question: Which traveler chose a better way, the humble one or the proud one?
questions.answer: The humble one chose the better way.

questions.question: What wise step did the humble traveler take?
questions.answer: He used the name of a tribal leader for protection.

questions.question: What was the result of using that leader’s name?
questions.answer: He traveled safely and was treated well.

questions.question: What mistake did the proud traveler make?
questions.answer: He depended only on himself.

questions.question: What did that mistake lead to?
questions.answer: It led to fear, hardship, and shame.

questions.question: Why does the passage speak to the nafs after the story?
questions.answer: To remind the person to stop being proud and turn to Allah.

questions.question: What does the passage say about our weakness and needs?
questions.answer: They are very great and never fully end.

questions.question: Whose name should a person take instead of depending on himself?
questions.answer: A person should take the name of Allah, the everlasting Lord.

questions.question: What two big things does this blessed phrase give to a weak person?
questions.answer: Strength and mercy.

questions.question: How is a person who says Allah’s name like a soldier?
questions.answer: He acts with support and authority, not alone.

questions.question: What feeling should a believer have after learning this passage?
questions.answer: The believer should feel trust in Allah and less fear.

questions.question: What short phrase is the passage teaching about?
questions.answer: It is teaching about saying “In the Name of Allah.”

questions.question: What kind of things should start with this phrase?
questions.answer: All good things should start with it.

questions.question: What does the passage say all creatures do in their own way?
questions.answer: They show this meaning by their natural state.

questions.question: What place is used in the story to help explain the lesson?
questions.answer: A desert in Arabia.

questions.question: Why could a person not travel safely there by himself?
questions.answer: Because there were too many dangers and needs.

questions.question: What were the two men alike in?
questions.answer: Both of them were on the same kind of journey.

questions.question: What were they unlike in?
questions.answer: One was humble, and one was full of pride.

questions.question: Which traveler found peace on the trip?
questions.answer: The humble traveler did.

questions.question: What protected the humble traveler from robbers?
questions.answer: Traveling under a leader’s name protected him.

questions.question: What does the proud traveler’s suffering teach us?
questions.answer: It teaches that pride and self-reliance bring trouble.

questions.question: What does the passage compare the world to?
questions.answer: It compares the world to a desert.

questions.question: What does it say about a human being’s power by himself?
questions.answer: It says a person is weak and needy by himself.

questions.question: What should a person do because he has many needs and enemies?
questions.answer: He should seek safety by using Allah’s name.

questions.question: How does the passage describe what this phrase becomes for us?
questions.answer: It becomes like a treasure of help and mercy.

questions.question: What change happens to weakness and need when linked to Allah?
questions.answer: They become a way to receive Allah’s mercy.

questions.question: If a child wanted to use this lesson today, what could he do before a task?
questions.answer: He could say Allah’s name before starting.

questions.question: According to the passage, what should come first when we begin something good?
questions.answer: Remembering Allah by saying His name should come first.

questions.question: What does the passage say this phrase shows about a person?
questions.answer: It shows the mark of being Muslim.

questions.question: To explain its power, what kind of example is given?
questions.answer: A travel story is given.

questions.question: How many travelers are in the story?
questions.answer: There are two travelers.

questions.question: What was the humble traveler like in character?
questions.answer: He was modest and not arrogant.

questions.question: What was the proud traveler like in character?
questions.answer: He was conceited and full of himself.

questions.question: Why did the humble traveler receive honor at the tents?
questions.answer: People respected the leader’s name he carried.

questions.question: What feelings filled the proud traveler on the road?
questions.answer: He felt fear and lowliness.

questions.question: What did the proud traveler have to do because he lacked protection?
questions.answer: He had to ask others for help.

questions.question: When the story is explained, who is being warned?
questions.answer: The nafs is being warned.

questions.question: What two hard facts about people are mentioned after the story?
questions.answer: People have endless weakness and endless needs.

questions.question: What does the passage say we should do because of those hard facts?
questions.answer: We should take Allah’s name and trust Him.

questions.question: What does this phrase connect us to besides power?
questions.answer: It connects us to mercy too.

questions.question: Why is the phrase compared to entering the army?
questions.answer: Because it shows acting with backing, order, and protection.

questions.question: What can such a person do bravely?
questions.answer: He can speak, act, and endure with confidence.

questions.question: What is better according to this passage: pride or humble trust in Allah?
questions.answer: Humble trust in Allah is better.

questions.question: What is the blessed beginning taught in this passage?
questions.answer: The blessed beginning is to say Allah’s name.

questions.question: What does the passage say this beginning is for Islam?
questions.answer: It is one of its signs.

questions.question: What lesson does the story try to show about this beginning?
questions.answer: It shows that it gives help, safety, and support.

questions.question: Where did the story happen?
questions.answer: It happened on a desert journey.

questions.question: Why was traveling there hard for a person alone?
questions.answer: There were many threats and many things he needed.

questions.question: What choice did the humble man make that the proud man did not?
questions.answer: He chose to travel under a chief’s name.

questions.question: What happened when the humble man met dangerous people?
questions.answer: He stayed safe from them.

questions.question: What happened when the proud man tried to continue on his own?
questions.answer: He went through many disasters and became miserable.

questions.question: Which traveler shows the better way for a believer?
questions.answer: The humble traveler shows the better way.

questions.question: What does the passage say the world is like?
questions.answer: It is like a desert journey.

questions.question: What are people like in that world if they rely only on themselves?
questions.answer: They are weak, needy, and easily afraid.

questions.question: Who is named as the true ruler and lord we should rely on?
questions.answer: Allah is the everlasting ruler and lord.

questions.question: What kind of storehouse is this phrase compared to?
questions.answer: It is compared to a blessed treasure.

questions.question: What does that treasure provide for a person?
questions.answer: It provides strength and mercy.

questions.question: What job example is used at the end of the passage?
questions.answer: The example of a soldier in the army is used.

questions.question: How is a believer like that soldier when acting with Allah’s name?
questions.answer: The believer acts with support and does not need to fear others.

questions.question: What simple habit does the passage teach for every good action?
questions.answer: Start it by saying Allah’s name.

questions.question: Why is this habit important for Muslims?
questions.answer: It is part of the way Islam is known and lived.

questions.question: What story form is used to make the lesson easy to understand?
questions.answer: A comparison story is used.

questions.question: What kind of land did the two men cross?
questions.answer: They crossed a desert land.

questions.question: What could help a traveler stay safe there?
questions.answer: Traveling under a leader’s protection could help.

questions.question: Which man accepted that protection?
questions.answer: The humble man accepted it.

questions.question: Which man refused that help?
questions.answer: The proud man refused it.

questions.question: What was one result for the humble man?
questions.answer: He moved about safely.

questions.question: What was one result for the proud man?
questions.answer: He suffered and felt scared.

questions.question: What does the desert journey teach us about life in this world?
questions.answer: Life has many dangers and needs, so we should not act as if we are enough by ourselves.

questions.question: What does the passage call the human condition in this world?
questions.answer: It calls us very weak and very needy.

questions.question: What should a person do to be saved from fear and begging?
questions.answer: He should rely on Allah by using His name.

questions.question: What two gifts come through this phrase according to the passage?
questions.answer: Power and mercy come through it.

questions.question: How does the passage explain that weakness can still be good?
questions.answer: When turned to Allah, weakness becomes a reason to receive help.

questions.question: Why does the soldier example fit this lesson well?
questions.answer: It shows how someone can act boldly when supported by a higher authority.

questions.question: What is the main message a 2nd grader should remember from this passage?
questions.answer: Don’t be proud and alone; begin with Allah’s name and trust Him.
